intentional_corrections: Turbine cold-side rejected heat excludes the electrical work; upstream adds all input heat to the cold side while also generating work
Reversed turbine polarity transports heat from the physically warmer reservoir
Furnace mode changes preserve its valid temperature target
Room door scanning handles its initial Long.MIN_VALUE timestamp without subtraction overflow
Thevenin probes restore the actual source setting so controller iterations do not erase unflushed source commands
Under-relax coupled solar source commands to converge when the original current clamp is active
Farming lamp random growth ticks target the crop intercepted by its illuminated ray rather than the original last non-air block, which can select farmland and fail to grow its crop

Explicitly register high projected-light sections and enable their light sources with the Minecraft light engine; a block reporting emission alone did not light previously empty sections in the headless world
Clutch coupling caps the original speed increment at its momentum-conserving intersection and records finite friction loss; stored energy cannot become negative or duplicate on reload
Radial intake smoothing retains consumed fuel heat in a finite saved chamber rather than letting the RC output produce unbacked power after the fuel empties
Gas and steam intake interpolation also retains finite consumed fluid heat, so a saved RC output cannot create unbacked shaft work after the tank empties
Original generator shaft cost divides electrical output by 95% efficiency; upstream multiplies by 95%, thereby creating energy
Motor/generator conversion and friction losses enter the thermal simulation as actual joules over elapsed time; upstream passes an energy quantity directly as thermal power
Motor/generator per-call drag is normalized to the original default 20 Hz electrical process cadence, so the native solver subdivisions do not increase physical friction
Rolling partial work persists across world reload, whereas the upstream StackMachineProcess has no NBT interface
Device timers survive a circuit graph rebuild; physical shaft placement is tracked separately from loading a saved shaft network, preventing false unsafe-merge explosions during chunk reload
Charge buffers receive integrated electrical work; original item capacities and per-interval transfer limits are bounded and shared across all sources, preventing NBT overfill or duplicated credit

Area/tree tools debit only accepted protected survival breaks, including the final 200 J block. Source extra-break logic can discard that final charge without harvesting; axe source also omits the initial log charge
Electrical item charge, boot counters and mode synchronization do not restart modern held-item equip animations or block breaking. Actual hotbar changes still animate
Broken scanner damage is bounded at its terminal state instead of wrapping its legacy byte back into a repaired device

Power antenna receiver output spends only a saved one-numerical-step field budget credited from actual transmitter resistor work; unused overflow dissipates, while incoming overload still reaches original receiver destruction.
Painted bus-to-bus connections keep corresponding channel indices; avoids the original accidental extra cross-channel connection when a bus itself was painted.

fullRegression.result: All required tests passed with published BCCE and CC.

latestFullAttempt.result: All required tests passed with published BCCE and CC.

nativeRegression.result: All required tests passed without optional mods.

remaining_verification_limits: The original development-only Conduit has no implemented source electrical/thermal function. It is excluded from ordinary equipment; the original deliberate Portable NaN debug item is replaced by isolated numerical fault-injection tests.

Legacy OpenComputers 1.7 APIs and IC2-only integration are not advertised as modern tested runtimes. The ComputerCraft probe is restored through optional CC: Tweaked 1.101.4; FE and the pinned BCCE native MJ bridge provide the tested energy adapters.

Original C-key node covers accept full collision-cube block models, including logs, glass, leaves and light-emitting blocks. Block entities, fluids and partial collision shapes are excluded. An unavailable mod cover retains its raw saved state and item data with a stone visual fallback.
Source creative prototypes remain identified as such. Registration counts and source recipe counts are not independent proof of functional completeness.
BCCE native linkage is pinned to published 8.0.23. Other BCCE versions and every engine/gate/machine combination are unverified. BCCE is not modified or embedded.

Client verification used an isolated integrated server and a QA-only host pacing agent. The agent and QA sources are excluded from the normal installable JAR. This is automated client testing, not a long manual survival/multiplayer campaign.

The component matrix distinguishes individual operating fixtures from implemented variants that share a tested runtime but have not been separately exercised. Broad modpack compatibility and every original localization/configuration option are not asserted.
